newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere up, banks firm in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere up, banks firm in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere shares rose on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Wednesday after weeks of stagnation and dealers said a surge by the company's Global Depositary Receipts in London stimulated the rise.
Two of the three listed bank shares also rose, strengthening the sector's leading position in the developing Lebanese equities market.
The LIBX bank index rose 0.66 percent to 137.7. The BLOM general index rose 0.96 percent to 928.99 and the LISPI rose 0.09 percent to 87.51.
Solidere A shares, the underlying shares of the company's GDRs, rose for the second consecutive day to $10.5 from $10.375 while B shares reached $10.875 from $10.75.
The rises ended a prolonged period during which the shares have stagnated close to their historic lows.
Georges Abou Jaoude of Financial Funds Advisors told Reuters the rise in the GDRs had stimulated the Solidere shares on the Beirut market.
"It's awakening peoples' minds on what we are doing with the Solidere shares here," he said. "The discount on the Solidere shares in Lebanon is so huge that it's unacceptable."

The GDRs, issued last November at $11.5, soared on the London Stock Exchange on Tuesday to $17.625 from last week's $12 and the company said purchases by U.S. and European emerging market funds were behind the increase.
Demand for A and B shares on Wednesday's first fixing totalled 252,788 shares against a supply of 124,736. This compared with demand of 75,022 shares against supply of 110,665 a day ealier.
However, Abou Jaoude said shares in Solidere, Lebanon's biggest company which is rebuilding central Beirut, would probably remain undervalued pending a Middle East settlement.
"Solidere needs something positive about peace in order to gather momentum and show its real value. Without peace or some indication of peace it can't reach its real value," he said.
Bank shares also met heavy demand. Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose 3.125 percent to $16.5 from $16, bringing its rise since listing last December to 46.66 percent.

Banque Audi rose to $20.125 from $20, the price at which it has been trading since April 15, after publishing first quarter results on Tuesday that financiers said were in line with its 1997 profit growth target of 20 percent.
Bank of Beirut fell to $3.5625 from $3.6, reducing its spectacular rise since its April 11 listing down to 64 percent from 66 percent.
Total BSE turnover was 298,316 against Tuesday's 367,010 and value was $2,667,156 against $2,513,622.
Among the four industrials, pipemaker Eternit fell to $1.8750 from $1.9375 and Ciments Libanais held steady at $1.2812. Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic UNI.BY were not traded.
